summary: Frontend-only regression test of the pure-extraction refactor for CalendarGridTab, MealEntryTab and MealMastersTab. Verified admin login, /admin/reports Calendar Grid, /admin/meals-report (Daily entry) and /admin/meals-report?tab=masters. All three screens load and their extracted sub-components render/behave correctly, EXCEPT one clear regression: an orphaned JSX comment fragment (`column widths as the grid below … */}`) is leaked as visible plain text at the top of the Daily-entry totals area — the opening `{/*` was lost during the refactor of MealEntryTab.jsx.

ui_bugs.issue: Orphaned JSX comment leaks into rendered UI. Lines read `column widths as the grid below, so each amount sits / directly above its column's item Amounts. Labels tuck to / the left of each band, numbers hang on the right rail. */}` with no opening `{/*`. This literal text now shows above the PURCHASES/ISSUES/WASTAGE Day-Total cards on /admin/meals-report (Daily entry). Introduced by the recent extraction refactor.
ui_bugs.selector: text=/column widths as the grid below/

verified_flows: Admin email login (admin@attendance.app) succeeds and reaches /.

/admin/reports → Calendar Grid tab: table renders 49 rows, 47 members, day columns 01..30, right-sticky totals (MSS, P TOTAL, AB DAYS, LP DAYS, LV TOTAL, TR TOTAL, OT SUM, EO DAYS, LT DAYS) present. Today's column (26 SA) shows a sky-blue vertical outline spanning the day-number header, weekday sub-header, and every body cell (visible in screenshot .screenshots/grid_final.png).

/admin/meals-report (default Daily entry) renders category groups (Fruits, Masalas and Herbs, Vegetables, Protein, Cleaning items, Dairy products, Gas, Fats, Dryfruits and Seeds, Greens, Lentils/Daal/Legumes, Carbs and Sugars) with per-category testids `entry-cat-header-<code>` and totals cards `entry-purchase-total-card`.
Double-clicking the 'PURCHASES · DAY TOTAL' card opens the Date-wise totals modal — [data-testid='daily-totals-modal'] appears and closes cleanly.

/admin/meals-report?tab=masters renders the Categories→Items tree with grand total row, category rows (masters-cat-<code>) and per-item rows exposing testids masters-item-unit-<id>, masters-item-opening-<id>, masters-item-min-<id>, masters-item-norm-<id>, masters-item-rename-btn-<id>, masters-item-nutrition-<id>. Search box (`masters-search`) is present.
Clicking the Nutrition (flame) button on an item opens the nutrition modal ([data-testid^='nutrition-modal-']) as expected.
not_fully_verified: RowVendorPicker '＋ Add new vendor…' → add-vendor-inline-modal flow: category expansion selector used in the script didn't match the `entry-cat-header-<code>` toggle testid, so vendor picker was not reached. Testids exist (entry-cat-header-*) so this appears to be a script selector gap, not a product bug. Recommend explicit test using entry-cat-header-fruits toggle + row-vendor-picker-<itemId>.

Inline rename editor on item rows: rename button click did not surface an input matching `input:focus`. Could be that the editor uses a contentEditable/span; visual verification via screenshot did not show an obvious editor. Worth a follow-up manual check.
Saving a Min-level inline number edit: intentionally NOT executed to avoid mutating live production data (per agent-to-agent note).
action_items: Fix MealEntryTab.jsx lines 848-851: restore the missing `{/*` opener (or delete the stranded comment) so the totals-bar comment stops leaking as visible text on the Daily-entry page. Suggested minimal patch: replace the blank line above with `{/* Totals bar — mirrors the same` (matching the original comment intent) so lines 848-851 form a valid `{/* … */}` block, or simply delete lines 849-851 and the stray `*/}`.
critical_code_review_comments: MealEntryTab.jsx (1354 lines) and MealMastersTab.jsx are still >700 lines even after the extraction — consider further splitting per the file-size code-review guideline.
Console shows an intermittent 503 on a resource load during Daily-entry render; not blocking but worth a look in logs.

The refactor did not introduce runtime errors (no PAGEERR captured), but the orphan-comment regression proves the need to add a simple lint/CI check (e.g. eslint-plugin-react no-unescaped-entities or a plain grep for `*/}` without matching `{/*`) to catch this class of extraction bug.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (1 clear UI regression, 2 flows partially verified)

seed_data_creation: None. No writes performed; live production data untouched per instruction.
context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent fixes the orphaned JSX comment in MealEntryTab.jsx (~lines 848-851), re-open /admin/meals-report and confirm the leaked text is gone. Then, to complete the vendor-picker path: click `[data-testid='entry-cat-header-fruits']` (or any category header) to expand items, then click any row-vendor-picker (search DOM for `data-testid^='row-vendor-picker'` — pattern likely `row-vendor-picker-<itemId>`), pick '＋ Add new vendor…' and assert `[data-testid='add-vendor-inline-modal']` opens. Also verify inline rename editor and a Min-level number edit round-trip on an obviously-test item (revert immediately).
rca of the issue: During the pure-extraction refactor of MealEntryTab, a JSX block comment `{/* … Totals bar column widths … */}` had its opening `{/*` accidentally removed when nearby JSX (likely the flags banner block ending on line 847) was reformatted. Because JSX renders unmatched text as a text node, the tail of the comment — three lines of prose plus `*/}` — is now shown to the user above the totals cards. Reproduction: log in as admin → /admin/meals-report → observe visible text `column widths as the grid below, so each amount sits directly above its column's item Amounts. Labels tuck to the left of each band, numbers hang on the right rail. */}` immediately below the toolbar and above the PURCHASES/ISSUES/WASTAGE totals cards (screenshot .screenshots/meals_landing.png). Mitigation: restore `{/*` before line 849 (or delete lines 849-851 outright). Zero behavior-change goal of the refactor is otherwise upheld — grid highlight, tree render, modals, and testids all work.
